sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Rice County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Deeds for land in Rice County are recorded by the County Recorder, who is also the Registrar of Titles. The office is in the Government Services Building at 320 Third St. NW in Faribault. The phone number is 507-332-6114.

The Recorder files documents for both Abstract and Torrens property, plus plats, federal and state tax liens, military discharges and more than 300 other document types. Staff accept, review, receipt, index and scan each filing, and paper or electronic submissions are both taken. The office does not give legal advice or help prepare documents, so a title company or attorney should draft the deed.

sections.h2: Is your Rice County property Abstract or Torrens?
sections.html:
Most Rice County property is Abstract, but you should confirm before a sale. Minnesota has two recording systems, and the paperwork differs between them.

With Abstract title, an abstract is a condensed history of every deed, mortgage and other document touching the land, and an attorney or title insurer reviews it. With Torrens title, a court directs issuance of a certificate of title, and the certificate itself is the title. The Recorder acts as Registrar of Titles and works with the Examiner of Titles, who advises the registrar. In Rice County the Examiner is Debbie Korman at 507-334-5534, 504 Central Ave. N, P.O. Box 716, Faribault.

The county publishes a Torrens property list, but it is only partial. The county's own advice is to complete a title search of the land records before deciding which system applies to a given parcel.

sections.h2: How can you get a document recorded in Rice County?
sections.html:
You can bring or mail a paper original to the Recorder, or send it electronically through one of the e-recording partners the county lists:

  • Simplifile, 800-460-5657.
  • CSCGlobal, 866-652-0111.
  • eRecording Partners (GOePN), 888-325-3365.
  • Indecomm Global Services, 877-272-5250.
  • Hopdox, 385-501-5103.

The county says recording means the document is reproduced and the original returned to the presenter, while filing means the office keeps the original. Deeds and mortgage releases are recorded. Anyone can view public records in the research area during business hours at no charge, and copies of recorded documents are $1.00 per page.

For online research, the Recorder has scanned 1,166 plats, 789,492 Abstract documents and 60,375 Torrens documents into LandShark. Access costs $50 a month plus $2 per document, with a $50 set-up fee.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Rice County?
sections.html:
Minnesota Statutes section 357.18 caps recorder fees, and the county follows that schedule. Rice County asks for recorder fees on one check made out to Rice County, and for deed tax and mortgage registry tax on a separate check, because the Property Tax & Elections department processes the tax.

Recording charges in Minnesota Statutes 357.18 and the Rice County Recorder FAQ

sections.h2: What taxes and certificates go with a Rice County deed?
sections.html:
State deed tax is set by section 287.21. When the net consideration is more than $3,000 the tax is .0033 of it, and when it is $3,000 or less, or the transfer has no consideration, the tax is $1.65. The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording.

Other items travel with the deed:

  • A certificate of real estate value for any sale over $3,000, which must include the Social Security or employer number of every grantor and grantee under section 272.115.
  • A well disclosure statement or certificate on a transfer for more than $3,000, using the Minnesota Department of Health form.
  • A drafting statement with the full name and address of the person who prepared the document.
  • The grantor's marital status, and the spouse's signature where required.
  • A notary acknowledgment that meets Minnesota Statutes section 359.03.

sections.h2: Why does the Rice County Recorder reject documents?
sections.html:
The county publishes two top ten lists of reasons for rejection, and several repeat in both. In the Abstract department the common ones are a missing well certificate or well statement, a missing drafting statement, no marital status, the wrong number for a document being satisfied or assigned, an incorrect recording fee, and a missing or incomplete certificate of real estate value. Taxes that are not current also lead to a rejection.

Torrens filings face a stricter test. The legal description and owner names must match the certificate of title exactly, cross reference numbers must be right, and a bank name change needs an extra $20 memorial fee. Every document must also meet the standards in Minnesota Statutes section 507.093. A rejected package costs you days, which matters when a closing date is fixed.

sections.h2: Do unpaid taxes block a deed in Rice County?
sections.html:
They can. Section 272.12 requires the county auditor to check for delinquent tax when a deed is presented, and the Recorder may not accept the deed without the auditor's note that no delinquent taxes are owed and the transfer is entered. Deeds of distribution in probate and transfer on death deeds are among the listed exceptions. Contact Rice County Property Tax & Elections at 507-332-6104 for a current balance before you schedule closing.

Faribault and Northfield are the county's two largest cities, and Northfield crosses into Dakota County. A parcel in that part of town is not recorded in Rice County, so check the county on the tax statement before you send anything.

sections.h2: What happens after a Rice County deed is recorded?
sections.html: The Recorder returns the original, and the title company or buyer arranges the next steps. The assessor removes homestead classification from a sold property for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies, under section 272.115. For context, Rice County had 25,596 housing units in July 2025 and 100 building permits in 2025, and 87.5% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, per the Census Bureau. Searching LandShark or visiting the research area is the quickest way to check what is already on your parcel.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a deed in Rice County?
faqs.a: $46, the amount set by Minnesota Statutes section 357.18 for indexing and recording a deed or similar instrument. State deed tax is a separate charge, paid on its own check.

faqs.q: Does Rice County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The county lists Simplifile, CSCGlobal, eRecording Partners, Indecomm Global Services and Hopdox as e-recording partners. The Recorder's number is 507-332-6114 if you need to know which fits your closing.

faqs.q: Can I look at Rice County land records for free?
faqs.a: Yes. The public research area at the Government Services Building in Faribault is open during business hours, and all public records can be viewed free. Copies cost $1.00 per page.

faqs.q: What is the Minnesota deed tax on a Rice County sale?
faqs.a: It is .0033 of the net consideration when that is above $3,000, and $1.65 when it is $3,000 or less. Section 287.21 sets this, and the tax is due at the time the deed is presented.

faqs.q: Can the Rice County Recorder help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says it does not give legal advice or help prepare documents. Staff can explain filing requirements, and a licensed attorney or title company should draft the deed.
